summary: Defines MIB objects for managing the Internet Group Management Protocol and Multicast Listener Discovery. They let network management tools monitor and configure how hosts join multicast groups.

eli5.summary: Computers join group broadcasts, like tuning to a radio channel, and routers track who is listening. This note defines the dials and counters for checking and adjusting that tracking.

subtitle: The SNMP management objects for watching and tuning IGMP and MLD on hosts and routers.

tldr.problem: Operators need a standard way to see and configure how hosts and routers track multicast group membership, for both IPv4 (IGMP) and IPv6 (MLD), including source filtering.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5519 defines the MGMD-STD-MIB module in SMIv2 with eight tables covering host and router interfaces, group caches, reverse lookups and source lists, registered as mib-2 185.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 2933 and RFC 3019 and merges them into one MIB for IGMP and MLD, adding objects for IGMPv3 and MLDv2 source filtering.

today: RFC 5519 is a Proposed Standard from April 2009 and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It obsoletes RFC 2933 and RFC 3019.

sections.title: Why One MIB for IGMP and MLD
sections.content:
RFC 5519 defines part of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP, versions 1 to 3) and Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD, versions 1 and 2). IGMP pertains to IPv4 clients and MLD to IPv6 clients, and both provide multicast membership discovery.

The RFC introduces a combined name, Multicast Group Membership Discovery (MGMD), for the two. It obsoletes RFC 2933 and RFC 3019, gives IGMP and MLD a generic interface, and adds changes to enable source filtering in multicast clients. The MIB covers both router and host nodes.
sections.eli5: There used to be two separate control panels for two kinds of group-listening. This memo builds one panel that works for both.

sections.title: The Management Framework
sections.content: MIB objects are generally accessed with the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and defined using the Structure of Management Information (SMI). The module here is compliant with SMIv2, described in STD 58 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580). It imports interface indexes from the Interfaces MIB (RFC 2863) and address types from RFC 4001.
sections.eli5: SNMP is the language network managers use to ask devices questions. The MIB is the list of questions a device understands.

sections.title: The Eight Tables
sections.content:
The MGMD MIB module contains eight tables. Each is meant for either router or host functionality.

  • The Host Interface and Router Interface tables hold one row per interface where IGMP or MLD is enabled.
  • The Host Cache and Router Cache tables hold one row per multicast group with members on an interface.
  • The two reverse (inverse) tables hold one row per interface that has active groups.
  • The HostSrcList and RouterSrcList tables hold one row per entry in the source filter record for an interface and group, and are supported only on IGMPv3 and MLDv2 nodes.

Interface tables are indexed by interface index plus address type (IPv4 or IPv6), because a physical interface may run both modes while the traffic is treated as logically separate. The MIB also includes objects for IGMP and MLD proxy devices, as described in RFC 4605.
sections.eli5: There are eight lists: who is on each connection, which groups they joined, and which senders they want or do not want.

sections.title: Host and Router Interface Settings
sections.content:
On a host, the Host Interface table reports the querier address and lets a manager set the maximum version the host runs (1 to 3, default 3). It also holds timers that show how long the host will keep answering as an older version, and a version 3 robustness value (default 2) that makes the host retransmit state-change reports robustness minus one times. Creating a row enables the host side on that interface and destroying it disables it.

On a router, the Router Interface table adds tunable parameters with these defaults:

  • Query interval: 125 seconds (range 1 to 31744).
  • Query max response time: 100 tenths of seconds.
  • Robustness: 2, meaning IGMP and MLD tolerate robustness minus one packet losses.
  • Last member query interval: 10 tenths of seconds, which affects leave latency.

There are also read-only objects such as the querier uptime and expiry time, a count of wrong-version queries (which signals a configuration error, since all routers on a LAN must run the same version), a count of joins, the number of groups, and an optional proxy interface index.
sections.eli5: These are the dials. They set how often the router asks who is listening and how patient it is before deciding someone left.

sections.title: Group Caches and Source Lists
sections.content:
The cache tables list each multicast group for an interface with an uptime and the address of the last reporter. They also show a source filter mode of include (1) or exclude (2). Router cache rows carry extra timers, such as expiry and per-version host timers.

The source list tables extend the caches by listing the source-specific includes or excludes for each group and interface, with an expiry for each entry. They are meaningful only on IGMPv3 and MLDv2 nodes. The RFC also defines several MODULE-COMPLIANCE statements, separately for host and router, read and write access, and the IGMP and MLD versions supported.
sections.eli5: The caches are the guest list. The source lists add notes like: only listen to this speaker, or listen to everyone except that one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some objects are read-write or read-create, and unprotected SET operations can hurt network operations. The RFC singles out the router interface status, which lets a remote user enable or disable multicast on an interface and is therefore a significant denial-of-service risk. The query interval, the router version, the max response time, robustness and the last member query interval are tuning controls whose compromise could disrupt local multicast. The host version 3 robustness object is described as low risk.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 lacked adequate security. The RFC RECOMMENDS SNMPv3 with its cryptographic authentication and privacy, says deploying older versions is NOT RECOMMENDED, and leaves it to the operator to give access only to legitimate users.
sections.eli5: If a stranger could turn the dials, they could switch off the group service. So the controls need a lock, and SNMPv3 is the lock.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The module uses the IANA-assigned object identifier mgmdStdMIB, { mib-2 185 }, recorded in the SMI Numbers registry. The section also notes that MGMD is a new term that covers both IGMP and MLD.
sections.eli5: The panel gets an official address number, 185, so every device finds it in the same place.
